root-canal.intro: Root canal therapy is a treatment used to address infection or damage to the pulp — the soft tissue inside a tooth containing nerves and blood vessels.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body:
Rather than removing the affected tooth, root canal therapy aims to remove the infected or damaged pulp, clean the internal canals, and seal the tooth, allowing it to be preserved wherever possible.

At Footscray Dental Studio, we use advanced root canal treatment technology to support precise, efficient treatment.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
Root canal therapy generally includes:

  1. Assessment — your dentist examines the tooth and takes an X-ray to assess the extent of infection or damage.
  2. Local anaesthetic — administered to ensure the area is numb and you remain comfortable throughout treatment.
  3. Access and cleaning — an opening is made to access the pulp chamber, and the infected or damaged pulp is removed. The canals are then cleaned and shaped.
  4. Filling the canal — the cleaned canals are filled with a biocompatible material to seal them.
  5. Restoration — the tooth is restored, often with a filling, and a crown may be recommended afterwards to protect and strengthen the tooth.

sections.heading: Signs You May Need Root Canal Therapy
sections.body:
• Persistent or severe toothache
  • Sensitivity to hot or cold that lingers after the stimulus is removed
  • Swelling or tenderness in the gums near a tooth
  • Darkening of a tooth
  • A recurring pimple-like bump on the gum

Not every case presents obvious symptoms, so a dental examination and X-ray are important for an accurate diagnosis.

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Root canal therapy may be recommended when the pulp inside a tooth becomes infected or inflamed, often due to deep decay, a crack, or trauma. It's generally aimed at patients who wish to preserve their natural tooth rather than have it extracted. Your dentist will assess whether root canal therapy is a suitable option for your specific tooth, or whether extraction and replacement may be more appropriate in some cases.

sections.heading: What to Expect Afterwards
sections.body:
Some mild discomfort or sensitivity is common in the days following treatment, which typically settles over time. Your dentist will provide guidance on managing this and will discuss whether a crown is recommended to protect the treated tooth going forward.

Book an AppointmentContact Us

faq.q: Is root canal therapy painful?
faq.a: Local anaesthetic is used throughout the procedure, and most patients find it no more uncomfortable than having a filling — your dentist will discuss pain management with you.

faq.q: How many visits does root canal therapy take?
faq.a: This depends on the complexity of the case and the tooth involved — your dentist will outline the expected number of visits during your consultation.

faq.q: Will I need a crown after root canal therapy?
faq.a: Often yes, particularly for back teeth, as a crown helps protect and strengthen the tooth following treatment — your dentist will advise based on your specific situation.

faq.q: What happens if I don't get root canal therapy for an infected tooth?
faq.a: Untreated infection can potentially worsen or spread — your dentist can discuss the risks relevant to your specific situation and the alternative of extraction.

faq.q: Can any tooth be treated with root canal therapy?
faq.a: Suitability depends on factors such as the extent of damage and the tooth's structure — your dentist will assess this using an examination and X-ray.

faq.q: How long does a root-canal-treated tooth last?
faq.a: With appropriate restoration and care, treated teeth can last many years — your dentist can discuss what to expect for your specific tooth.

fillings.intro: When a tooth is affected by decay, a filling is one of the most common ways to restore it — removing the decayed portion of the tooth and replacing it with a durable material to restore shape, function and appearance.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: At Footscray Dental Studio, we use tooth-coloured composite fillings, designed to blend naturally with your surrounding teeth.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
A typical filling appointment includes:

  1. Assessment — your dentist examines the affected tooth, often supported by an X-ray, to determine the extent of decay.
  2. Local anaesthetic — administered as needed to ensure your comfort during treatment.
  3. Removal of decay — the decayed portion of the tooth is carefully removed.
  4. Filling placement — the tooth-coloured composite material is applied in layers and shaped to match the natural contour of your tooth.
  5. Curing and finishing — each layer is hardened using a curing light, then polished and checked against your bite.

sections.heading: Signs You May Need a Filling
sections.body:
• Visible holes or dark spots on a tooth
  • Sensitivity to hot, cold or sweet foods
  • Pain when biting or chewing
  • A tooth that feels rough or has a noticeable chip

Not all decay causes obvious symptoms, which is one reason regular check-ups and X-rays are important for catching issues early.

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Fillings are suitable for most patients with tooth decay that hasn't progressed to affect the tooth's nerve. For more extensive damage or infection, your dentist may recommend an alternative treatment such as a crown or root canal therapy, which they'll discuss with you following assessment.

sections.heading: Caring for a Filled Tooth
sections.body:
Filled teeth are cared for in the same way as your natural teeth — regular brushing, flossing, and check-ups help monitor the filling's condition over time and catch any new decay early.

Book an AppointmentContact Us

faq.q: Does getting a filling hurt?
faq.a: Local anaesthetic is used as needed, and most patients find the procedure comfortable — your dentist will discuss pain management options with you.

faq.q: How long do composite fillings last?
faq.a: Longevity varies depending on the size of the filling, its location, and individual factors such as oral hygiene and diet — your dentist can advise what to expect for your specific filling.

faq.q: Will my filling match the colour of my tooth?
faq.a: Yes, composite fillings are tooth-coloured and shade-matched to blend with your natural teeth.

faq.q: How do I know if I need a filling?
faq.a: Common signs include visible holes, sensitivity or pain, though decay isn't always noticeable without an examination or X-ray — regular check-ups help catch this early.

faq.q: Can old fillings be replaced?
faq.a: Yes, older fillings can be assessed and replaced if needed — your dentist will advise if this is recommended during your check-up.

faq.q: How long does a filling appointment take?
faq.a: This depends on the size and location of the filling — your dentist can give you a more specific estimate at your appointment.

dentures.intro: Dentures are removable appliances used to replace missing teeth, restoring function for eating and speaking, as well as supporting facial structure and appearance.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: At Footscray Dental Studio, we provide both full dentures, for patients missing all teeth in an arch, and partial dentures, for patients missing some but not all of their natural teeth.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
The denture process generally includes:

  1. Consultation and assessment — your dentist examines your mouth and discusses whether full or partial dentures are appropriate for your situation.
  2. Impressions or digital scan — used to capture the precise shape of your mouth and any remaining teeth.
  3. Try-in stage — a trial denture may be fitted to check appearance, fit and bite before the final version is completed.
  4. Fitting — your finished dentures are fitted, with adjustments made as needed for comfort.
  5. Follow-up — further adjustment appointments may be recommended as you adapt to wearing your new dentures.

sections.heading: Types of Dentures
sections.body:
• Full dentures — replace all teeth in the upper and/or lower jaw, resting on the gums.
  • Partial dentures — replace one or more missing teeth while remaining natural teeth are still present, often attaching to adjacent teeth for stability.

Your dentist will discuss which option is suitable based on your remaining teeth and overall oral health.

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Dentures may be suitable for patients missing some or all of their natural teeth who are looking for a removable solution. For some patients, implant-supported options may also be discussed as an alternative or complement to dentures — your dentist will explain the options relevant to your individual situation.

sections.heading: Caring for Your Dentures
sections.body:
Your dentist will provide specific guidance on cleaning and caring for your dentures, including recommendations around removing them overnight, and will advise on a schedule for check-ups to monitor fit and the health of your gums and any remaining teeth over time.

Book a ConsultationContact Us

faq.q: How long does it take to get dentures?
faq.a: This depends on the type of denture and number of appointments required — your dentist will outline an expected timeframe during your consultation.

faq.q: Will dentures feel natural right away?
faq.a: Most patients need a short adjustment period when they first start wearing dentures — your dentist can offer guidance to help with this transition.

faq.q: How long do dentures last?
faq.a: Denture longevity varies depending on wear and changes in your mouth over time — your dentist will advise on when adjustments or replacement may be needed.

faq.q: Can I eat normally with dentures?
faq.a: Many patients adjust to eating a wide range of foods over time — your dentist can offer guidance on adapting during the initial period.

faq.q: What's the difference between dentures and implants?
faq.a: Dentures are removable, while implants are permanently anchored into the jawbone — your dentist can discuss which option, or combination, suits your situation.

faq.q: Do dentures need to be removed at night?
faq.a: Your dentist will provide specific guidance based on your denture type, though removing dentures overnight is commonly recommended to allow your gums to rest.

dental-implants.intro: Dental implants are a long-term option for replacing missing teeth, consisting of a titanium post surgically placed into the jawbone, which acts as an artificial tooth root.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body:
Once integrated with the bone, a custom crown or bridge can be attached, restoring both function and appearance.

If you're missing most or all of your teeth in an upper or lower jaw, you may also want to explore All-on-X Dental Implants, our full-arch implant solution.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
The dental implant process generally includes:

  1. Consultation and assessment — including a discussion of your goals and a clinical examination, often supported by X-rays or a scan to assess bone structure.
  2. Treatment planning — your dentist develops a plan tailored to your situation, which may involve referral to or collaboration with a specialist for the surgical placement.
  3. Implant placement — the titanium implant post is placed into the jawbone under local anaesthetic.
  4. Healing period — a period of healing allows the implant to integrate with the surrounding bone (a process known as osseointegration).
  5. Restoration — once healed, a custom crown or bridge is attached to the implant, completing the restoration.

sections.heading: Benefits of Dental Implants
sections.body:
• Designed to function similarly to a natural tooth root
  • Doesn't rely on adjacent teeth for support, unlike a traditional bridge
  • Can help maintain jawbone structure in the area of the missing tooth
  • Restorations are custom-made to match your natural teeth

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body:
Dental implants may be suitable for patients missing one or more teeth who have sufficient bone density and good general oral health to support the implant. Certain factors — such as smoking, some medical conditions, or insufficient bone volume — may affect suitability, which your dentist will assess during your consultation. Where bone volume is a concern, additional procedures may be discussed as part of your treatment plan.

For patients missing most or all of their teeth in an arch, our All-on-X Dental Implants page may be more relevant.

sections.heading: What to Expect During Recovery
sections.body:
Some swelling or discomfort is common in the days following implant placement, which your dentist will help you manage. A healing period is required before the final restoration is attached, allowing time for the implant to properly integrate with the jawbone.

Book an Implant ConsultationContact Us

faq.q: How long does the dental implant process take?
faq.a: This varies depending on individual healing time and the complexity of your treatment plan — your dentist will provide an estimated timeline during your consultation.

faq.q: Is getting a dental implant painful?
faq.a: The procedure is carried out under local anaesthetic, and your dentist will discuss pain management for the recovery period, which varies by individual.

faq.q: Am I a suitable candidate for dental implants?
faq.a: Suitability depends on factors such as bone density, gum health, and general health — this is assessed during a consultation, which is complimentary at Footscray Dental Studio.

faq.q: How long do dental implants last?
faq.a: With appropriate care and maintenance, implants are designed for long-term use — your dentist can discuss what to expect based on your individual circumstances.

faq.q: Do you place implants in-house or refer to a specialist?
faq.a: Please contact our team to confirm current arrangements, as some aspects of implant treatment may involve collaboration with a specialist depending on case complexity.

faq.q: What if I'm missing most or all of my teeth?
faq.a: For patients missing most or all of their teeth in an arch, All-on-X may be a more suitable option — see our dedicated All-on-X page for details.

crowns-bridges.intro: Crowns and bridges are custom-made restorations used to protect, strengthen or replace teeth. A crown covers and protects a damaged or weakened tooth, while a bridge replaces one or more missing teeth by anchoring to the surrounding teeth.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: Both are designed to restore function and blend naturally with your smile.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
Dental Crowns

  1. Assessment — your dentist examines the tooth and discusses whether a crown is the appropriate treatment.
  2. Preparation — the tooth is shaped to accommodate the crown, removing any decayed or damaged material.
  3. Digital scan or impression — used to fabricate a crown that fits precisely.
  4. Temporary crown — may be fitted while your permanent crown is being made, if fabricated off-site.
  5. Fitting — your custom crown is fitted, checked for comfort and bite, and permanently cemented into place.

Dental Bridges

  1. Assessment — your dentist assesses the gap and the health of the surrounding teeth that will support the bridge.
  2. Preparation — the supporting teeth are prepared to hold the bridge.
  3. Digital scan or impression — used to fabricate a bridge custom-fitted to your bite.
  4. Fitting — the bridge is fitted, checked, and cemented into place.

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body:
• Crowns may be recommended for teeth that are cracked, heavily decayed, worn, or following root canal treatment, where a filling alone wouldn't provide sufficient strength or protection.
  • Bridges may be recommended for patients missing one or more teeth who have healthy, suitable teeth on either side of the gap to support the bridge. For patients without suitable supporting teeth, or who prefer not to prepare adjacent healthy teeth, a dental implant may be discussed as an alternative.

Your dentist will assess your individual situation and discuss which option is most suitable.

sections.heading: Caring for Crowns & Bridges
sections.body:
Crowns and bridges are cared for like natural teeth — regular brushing and flossing, along with check-ups, help your dentist monitor their condition and the health of the supporting teeth and gums underneath.

Book a ConsultationContact Us

faq.q: How long do crowns and bridges last?
faq.a: Longevity varies by individual factors such as oral hygiene, bite forces and material used — your dentist can discuss what to expect for your specific restoration.

faq.q: Does getting a crown or bridge hurt?
faq.a: Local anaesthetic is used during preparation, and most patients find the process manageable — your dentist will explain what to expect for your treatment.

faq.q: How many visits does it take to get a crown or bridge?
faq.a: This depends on whether your crown or bridge is fabricated on-site or by an external laboratory — your dentist will explain the expected timeline during your consultation.

faq.q: What's the difference between a bridge and an implant?
faq.a: A bridge replaces a missing tooth by anchoring to the neighbouring teeth, while an implant is anchored directly into the jawbone without involving adjacent teeth — your dentist can discuss which suits your situation.

faq.q: Can a crown be placed on a tooth that's had a root canal?
faq.a: Yes, a crown is often recommended following root canal treatment to protect and strengthen the tooth.

faq.q: What materials are used for crowns and bridges?
faq.a: Your dentist can discuss the material options suitable for your specific situation, based on the location and function of the tooth involved.

all-on-x-implants.intro: For patients missing most or all of their teeth in an upper or lower jaw, All-on-X is a full-arch implant solution that uses a small number of strategically placed implants — typically four or more, hence "All-on-X" — to support a complete arch of replacement teeth.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: This approach is designed to provide a fixed, functional alternative to a removable full denture.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
All-on-X treatment generally includes:

  1. Comprehensive consultation and assessment — a detailed discussion of your goals, dental history and general health, along with imaging such as an OPG or CT scan to assess jawbone structure.
  2. Treatment planning — your dentist develops an individualised plan, which may involve collaboration with a specialist for the surgical stages.
  3. Implant placement — a small number of implants are strategically positioned across the arch to provide stable support for the full-arch restoration.
  4. Healing period — time is needed for the implants to integrate with the jawbone (osseointegration), during which a temporary restoration may be worn.
  5. Final restoration — once healing is complete, a custom-made full-arch restoration is fitted and secured to the implants.

Your dentist will explain the specific staging and expected timeframe for your individual treatment plan during your consultation.

sections.heading: Benefits of All-on-X
sections.body:
• A fixed alternative to a removable full denture, rather than a removable one
  • Uses a smaller number of implants to support a full arch, compared with replacing every tooth individually
  • Designed to restore function for eating and speaking, along with appearance
  • Can help support facial structure by providing stability similar to natural teeth

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: All-on-X may be an option for patients missing most or all of their teeth in one or both jaws, including those currently wearing a full denture who are looking for a fixed alternative. Suitability depends on individual factors including bone structure, gum health, and general health, all of which your dentist will assess during a comprehensive consultation. Where bone volume is insufficient, your dentist will discuss what options may be available.

sections.heading: What to Expect During Recovery
sections.body:
As with individual implants, some swelling or discomfort is common following surgical placement, and your dentist will provide guidance on managing this. A healing period is required before your final full-arch restoration is fitted, during which a temporary restoration may be worn to support function and appearance.

Book an All-on-X ConsultationContact Us

faq.q: What does "All-on-X" mean?
faq.a: "All-on-X" refers to a full arch of replacement teeth supported by a small number of implants — the "X" reflects the number of implants used, typically four or more, depending on your individual treatment plan.

faq.q: How is All-on-X different from individual dental implants?
faq.a: Individual implants typically replace one or a few missing teeth, while All-on-X uses a small number of implants to support a full arch of replacement teeth for patients missing most or all of their teeth.

faq.q: Am I a suitable candidate for All-on-X?
faq.a: Suitability depends on factors such as bone density, gum health, and general health — this is assessed during a comprehensive consultation, which is complimentary at Footscray Dental Studio.

faq.q: Is All-on-X treatment painful?
faq.a: The surgical placement is carried out under anaesthetic, and your dentist will discuss pain management for the recovery period, which varies by individual.

faq.q: How long does the All-on-X process take from start to finish?
faq.a: This varies depending on individual healing time and treatment planning — your dentist will provide an estimated timeline during your consultation.

faq.q: Can I switch from dentures to All-on-X?
faq.a: Many patients considering All-on-X are current denture wearers looking for a fixed alternative — your dentist can discuss whether this is a suitable option for your situation.

restorative.intro: Restorative dentistry focuses on repairing damaged, decayed or missing teeth to restore comfort, function and confidence.

sections.heading: What to Expect at Footscray Dental Studio
sections.body:
Whether you need a simple filling or a more involved treatment such as dental implants, our team takes an individualised approach — assessing your specific situation and explaining your options clearly before recommending a course of treatment.

Restorative treatment begins with a thorough assessment, often supported by digital X-rays or an OPG scan to understand the full picture of your oral health. Your dentist will explain what's involved, the expected timeframe, and any alternatives available, so you can make an informed decision about your care.

sections.heading: A Considered Approach to Restorative Care
sections.body:
Because restorative treatment can range from straightforward to more complex, we take the time to explain your options clearly, including any alternatives, so you can weigh up what's right for your situation, timeframe and budget.

Book a ConsultationContact Us

faq.q: How do I know which restorative treatment I need?
faq.a: This depends on your specific dental concern — your dentist will assess your teeth, often supported by X-rays, and recommend the most suitable option.

faq.q: Are restorative treatments covered by health funds?
faq.a: Many restorative treatments are covered to some extent by private health insurance — coverage depends on your individual policy.

faq.q: Is restorative treatment painful?
faq.a: Modern restorative dentistry, including the use of local anaesthetic where appropriate, is generally well tolerated — your dentist will explain what to expect for your specific treatment.

faq.q: Can I have sedation for restorative treatment?
faq.a: Please discuss sedation options with our team directly, as suitability depends on the treatment and your individual circumstances.

faq.q: How long do restorative treatments last?
faq.a: This varies by treatment type and individual factors such as oral hygiene — your dentist can discuss what to expect for your specific situation.

faq.q: Do I need a referral for implants or root canal therapy?
faq.a: No referral is generally needed to book a consultation — your dentist will advise if referral to a specialist is appropriate following assessment.

mouthguards.intro: Off-the-shelf mouthguards can feel bulky, ill-fitting, and are often left in a sports bag rather than worn when they're needed most.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: Custom-fitted mouthguards, made specifically for your teeth, offer a level of comfort, fit and protection that generic alternatives generally can't match. At Footscray Dental Studio, we provide custom mouthguards for sport, as well as night guards designed for patients who grind or clench their teeth during sleep.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
The process for a custom mouthguard or night guard typically includes:

  1. Assessment — your dentist discusses your needs, whether for sport, teeth grinding, or both.
  2. Digital scan or impression — a digital scan or physical impression of your teeth is taken to capture an accurate model of your mouth.
  3. Custom fabrication — your mouthguard is made to fit your teeth precisely, using this model.
  4. Fitting — your dentist checks the fit and comfort of the finished mouthguard and makes adjustments if needed.

sections.heading: Sport Mouthguards
sections.body: Custom sport mouthguards are recommended for patients, including children and teenagers, participating in contact or high-impact sports. A well-fitted mouthguard can be worn more comfortably and consistently than a generic option, which matters since protection is only effective when a mouthguard is actually worn during play.

sections.heading: Night Guards for Teeth Grinding (Bruxism)
sections.body: Night guards are recommended for patients experiencing teeth grinding or clenching, a condition known as bruxism. This often occurs during sleep and can contribute to worn or damaged teeth, jaw discomfort, and headaches over time. Your dentist can help identify signs of bruxism during a check-up and discuss whether a night guard is appropriate for you.

sections.heading: Benefits of Custom-Fitted Mouthguards
sections.body:
• Fit precisely to your teeth for improved comfort compared with generic options
  • Can be worn more consistently due to improved comfort and fit
  • Designed to accommodate your specific bite and dental structure
  • Suitable for a wide range of sports and for managing teeth grinding
  • Can be adjusted or remade as needed, including for growing children

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body:
• Sport mouthguards — recommended for patients, including children and teenagers, participating in contact or high-impact sports
  • Night guards — recommended for patients experiencing teeth grinding or clenching, which your dentist can help identify during a check-up

sections.heading: Caring for Your Mouthguard
sections.body:
Your dentist will provide guidance on cleaning and storing your mouthguard to help it last, along with when it may need to be checked or replaced — particularly important for children whose mouths are still developing.

Book an AppointmentContact Us

faq.q: Are custom mouthguards better than store-bought ones?
faq.a: Custom mouthguards are made to fit your teeth precisely, generally offering better comfort and protection than generic, off-the-shelf alternatives, and are more likely to be worn consistently.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a custom mouthguard?
faq.a: Turnaround time can vary depending on fabrication — our team can confirm timing when you book your appointment.

faq.q: Do children need custom mouthguards for sport?
faq.a: Yes, children participating in contact sports can benefit from a custom-fitted mouthguard, and we can accommodate growing or changing teeth with periodic remakes.

faq.q: How do I know if I need a night guard?
faq.a: Signs of teeth grinding include jaw soreness, headaches, or visible tooth wear — your dentist can assess this during a check-up and discuss whether a night guard would help.

faq.q: How often should a mouthguard be replaced?
faq.a: This depends on wear, growth (for children), and changes to your teeth over time — your dentist will advise at your regular check-ups.

faq.q: Can I use the same mouthguard for multiple sports?
faq.a: In most cases, yes — let your dentist know what activities you need it for so they can advise on the most suitable design.

gum-disease-care.intro: Healthy gums are just as important as healthy teeth, providing the foundation that supports your teeth in place.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body:
Gum disease develops in stages — starting with gingivitis, an early, generally reversible inflammation of the gums, which can progress to periodontitis if left untreated, potentially affecting the bone and tissue supporting your teeth. Regular check-ups allow your dentist to identify early changes and recommend appropriate care before the condition progresses.

At Footscray Dental Studio, gum health is assessed as a standard part of every check-up, with treatment tailored to the stage and severity of any gum disease present.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
Depending on your individual assessment, gum disease care may involve:

  1. Assessment — your dentist examines your gums for signs of inflammation, bleeding, recession or pocket depth around the teeth.
  2. Professional cleaning — removal of plaque and tartar build-up, including below the gumline where relevant.
  3. Home care guidance — practical advice on brushing, flossing and other techniques to improve gum health day-to-day.
  4. Ongoing monitoring — your gum health is reviewed at subsequent visits to track progress and adjust care as needed.
  5. Referral where appropriate — for more advanced periodontal disease, your dentist may recommend referral to a periodontist for specialised treatment.

sections.heading: Benefits of Early Gum Disease Care
sections.body:
• Gingivitis is generally reversible with timely professional care and improved home hygiene
  • Early intervention can help prevent progression to more serious periodontal disease
  • Supports long-term retention of your natural teeth
  • Reduces the risk of bone and tissue loss associated with advanced gum disease
  • Contributes to overall oral comfort and confidence

sections.heading: Signs of Gum Disease to Watch For
sections.body:
• Bleeding gums, particularly when brushing or flossing
  • Red, swollen or tender gums
  • Persistent bad breath
  • Gums that appear to be receding, making teeth look longer
  • Loose or shifting teeth (a sign of more advanced disease)

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Gum disease care is relevant to any patient showing signs of gingivitis or periodontal disease. Regular check-ups help identify these signs early, often before they're noticeable to the patient themselves, which is one of the key reasons routine visits are recommended even without symptoms.

sections.heading: Supporting Healthy Gums Long-Term
sections.body:
Good home care plays an important role in maintaining gum health between visits, including:

  • Brushing gently but thoroughly, twice daily
  • Daily flossing or interdental cleaning
  • Avoiding tobacco use, which is a significant risk factor for gum disease
  • Attending regular check-ups so changes can be caught early
Book an AppointmentContact Us

faq.q: What are the early signs of gum disease?
faq.a: Common signs include bleeding gums, swelling, and sensitivity, though your dentist can identify early changes during examination that aren't yet noticeable to you.

faq.q: Is gum disease reversible?
faq.a: Early-stage gum disease (gingivitis) can often be managed effectively with improved home care and professional cleaning; more advanced periodontal disease may require ongoing management rather than a complete reversal.

faq.q: How often should my gum health be checked?
faq.a: Gum health is typically assessed as part of your regular six-monthly check-up, though your dentist may recommend more frequent monitoring if you have existing gum concerns.

faq.q: Does gum disease treatment hurt?
faq.a: Your dentist will discuss what to expect based on your specific treatment plan and can take steps to help manage any discomfort during treatment.

faq.q: Can gum disease affect my overall health?
faq.a: Your dentist can discuss the relationship between oral and general health as it relates to your individual circumstances during your consultation.

faq.q: Will I be referred to a specialist for gum disease?
faq.a: Depending on severity, your dentist may recommend ongoing care in-house or referral to a periodontist for more advanced periodontal treatment.

fluoride-treatments.intro: Fluoride is a naturally occurring mineral that helps strengthen tooth enamel and supports resistance to acid attacks from plaque bacteria and sugars — one of the main contributors to tooth decay.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body:
While fluoride toothpaste provides everyday protection, professional fluoride treatments deliver a more concentrated application, offering an added layer of preventive care for patients at higher risk of decay.

At Footscray Dental Studio, we offer professional fluoride treatments as part of our preventive dentistry services, tailored to the needs of each patient.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
A professional fluoride treatment typically involves:

  1. Assessment — your dentist reviews your oral health and decay risk to determine whether fluoride treatment is appropriate.
  2. Preparation — your teeth are usually cleaned beforehand, often as part of your regular check-up and clean.
  3. Application — a concentrated fluoride gel, foam or varnish is applied directly to the teeth.
  4. Aftercare guidance — your dentist will let you know if there's a recommended waiting period before eating or drinking.

The process is quick, straightforward and generally well tolerated by both children and adults.

sections.heading: Benefits of Fluoride Treatment
sections.body:
• Helps strengthen tooth enamel against decay
  • Can help reduce sensitivity in some patients
  • Supports children's developing teeth as they emerge
  • A simple, non-invasive addition to routine preventive care
  • May help reduce the risk of future cavities, particularly in higher-risk patients

sections.heading: Who May Benefit Most
sections.body:
Fluoride treatments may be particularly recommended for:

  • Children as their teeth develop
  • Patients with a history of frequent cavities
  • Patients with dry mouth (reduced saliva flow)
  • Patients undergoing orthodontic treatment, where plaque control can be more difficult
  • Patients with early signs of enamel demineralisation

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Fluoride treatments may be recommended for children as their teeth develop, as well as adults with a higher risk of tooth decay. Your dentist will advise whether fluoride treatment is appropriate for you as part of your individual care plan.

sections.heading: What to Expect Afterwards
sections.body:
Your dentist may recommend avoiding eating or drinking for a short period following treatment to allow the fluoride to be fully absorbed — they'll let you know what applies to your specific treatment.

Book an AppointmentContact Us

faq.q: Is fluoride treatment only for children?
faq.a: No, fluoride treatments can also be recommended for adults, particularly those with a higher risk of tooth decay, dry mouth, or sensitivity.

faq.q: How often is fluoride treatment recommended?
faq.a: This varies by individual — your dentist will advise a schedule based on your oral health needs and risk factors.

faq.q: Does fluoride treatment hurt?
faq.a: No, it's a quick, non-invasive procedure typically applied during a routine check-up, with no discomfort involved.

faq.q: Can I eat or drink straight after treatment?
faq.a: Your dentist will let you know if there's a recommended waiting period after your specific treatment to allow it to take full effect.

faq.q: Is fluoride treatment covered by health funds?
faq.a: Coverage depends on your individual policy — check with your health fund or ask our team when you book.

faq.q: Can fluoride treatment be combined with a check-up and clean?
faq.a: Yes, it's commonly provided as part of the same visit as your regular check-up and clean for convenience.

fissure-sealants.intro: The chewing surfaces of your back teeth (molars and premolars) contain natural grooves and pits, known as fissures.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body:
These areas can be deep and narrow enough that a toothbrush bristle can't fully clean them, making them particularly vulnerable to decay. Fissure sealants are a thin, protective coating applied to these surfaces, acting as a barrier against plaque and food particles.

At Footscray Dental Studio, fissure sealants form part of our preventive approach, particularly for children as their adult molars come through.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
Applying a fissure sealant is a quick, straightforward process:

  1. Cleaning and preparation — the tooth surface is thoroughly cleaned and dried.
  2. Application — a liquid sealant material is applied into the grooves of the tooth.
  3. Setting — the sealant is hardened, often using a special curing light, forming a smooth protective layer.
  4. Check — your dentist checks your bite to ensure the sealant feels comfortable.

No drilling or anaesthetic is required, making it a comfortable option, including for younger patients.

sections.heading: Benefits of Fissure Sealants
sections.body:
• Creates a protective barrier over hard-to-clean tooth surfaces
  • Quick and painless to apply, with no drilling involved
  • Can reduce the risk of decay in molars and premolars
  • Particularly useful for children as their adult teeth emerge
  • A cost-effective, preventive alternative to treating decay after it occurs

sections.heading: Who May Benefit Most
sections.body:
Fissure sealants are commonly recommended for:

  • Children, as their permanent molars erupt (generally around ages 6 and 12)
  • Patients with deep grooves or pits in their back teeth
  • Patients with a history of decay in molars or premolars
  • Adults at higher risk of decay who haven't previously had sealants applied

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Fissure sealants are commonly recommended for children as their adult molars come through, though they may also be suitable for adults at higher risk of decay in these areas. Your dentist will advise if sealants are appropriate for you or your child during an examination.

sections.heading: Caring for Sealed Teeth
sections.body:
Sealants support—but don't replace—good oral hygiene. Continued brushing, flossing and regular check-ups remain important, and your dentist will monitor the condition of sealants at future visits.

Book an AppointmentContact Us

faq.q: At what age are fissure sealants usually applied?
faq.a: They're commonly applied as children's adult molars erupt, typically around ages 6 and 12, though the right timing depends on individual dental development.

faq.q: Are fissure sealants only for children?
faq.a: No, adults at higher risk of decay in these areas may also be suitable candidates, depending on individual assessment.

faq.q: Does the process hurt?
faq.a: No, applying fissure sealants is quick and non-invasive, with no drilling or anaesthetic required.

faq.q: How long do fissure sealants last?
faq.a: Your dentist will monitor sealants at regular check-ups and let you know if they need attention or reapplication over time, as wear can vary between patients.

faq.q: Do sealants replace the need for brushing and flossing?
faq.a: No, sealants are an additional preventive measure and don't replace regular oral hygiene at home.

faq.q: Can sealants be applied during a regular check-up visit?
faq.a: Yes, they're commonly applied as part of a routine preventive visit, making it a convenient addition to your check-up.

digital-xrays.intro: Accurate diagnosis is one of the most important parts of effective dental care — and much of what affects your oral health isn't visible to the naked eye.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body:
Decay between teeth, issues below the gum line, bone health, and the position of unerupted teeth all require imaging to assess properly. At Footscray Dental Studio, we use digital X-ray technology to capture detailed images quickly and efficiently, helping your dentist make well-informed decisions about your care.

Digital X-rays produce images almost instantly, using significantly less radiation than traditional film X-rays, and can be viewed and enlarged on-screen so your dentist can talk you through exactly what they show.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
Diagnostic imaging at our practice may include:

  1. Bitewing X-rays — used to check for decay between teeth and monitor bone levels around teeth.
  2. Periapical X-rays — focused images of a specific tooth, from crown to root tip, often used when investigating pain or infection.
  3. OPG (Orthopantomogram) imaging — a panoramic view capturing the entire jaw, teeth and surrounding structures in a single image, useful for broader assessments including wisdom teeth, jaw joints, and treatment planning.
  4. Intraoral camera images — small camera-captured images of the mouth used alongside X-rays to give a complete picture of your oral health.

Your dentist will explain which type of imaging is appropriate for your specific situation and why.

sections.heading: Benefits of Digital X-Rays
sections.body:
• Significantly lower radiation exposure compared with traditional film X-rays
  • Immediate results, viewable on-screen during your appointment
  • Greater diagnostic accuracy for issues not visible during a standard exam
  • Images can be enlarged and reviewed together with your dentist
  • Supports more precise treatment planning for procedures such as root canal therapy, implants, and orthodontics

sections.heading: When X-Rays May Be Recommended
sections.body: Your dentist may recommend diagnostic imaging if you're experiencing dental pain, as part of a new patient examination, before certain treatments (such as implants, root canal therapy, or wisdom tooth assessment), or as part of your regular preventive check-up schedule.

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: X-rays are recommended based on individual clinical need, which your dentist will assess as part of your check-up or treatment planning. This applies to patients of all ages, with imaging tailored to each person's specific requirements.

sections.heading: What to Expect
sections.body:
The process is quick, non-invasive and generally comfortable. Your dentist or dental assistant will position the equipment carefully and let you know what to expect beforehand. Images are available for review within moments.

Book an AppointmentContact Us

faq.q: Are digital X-rays safe?
faq.a: Digital X-rays use significantly less radiation than traditional film X-rays and are a standard, widely used diagnostic tool in modern dentistry.

faq.q: How often will I need X-rays?
faq.a: This depends on your individual dental history, risk factors and current concerns, as assessed by your dentist — not every visit requires new imaging.

faq.q: Can I see the X-ray images?
faq.a: Yes, digital X-rays can be viewed on-screen immediately, and your dentist can walk you through what they show as part of your consultation.

faq.q: What's the difference between a standard X-ray and an OPG?
faq.a: A standard X-ray (bitewing or periapical) focuses on a specific tooth or area, while an OPG (panoramic) image captures a broader view of the entire jaw, teeth and surrounding structures.

faq.q: Do children need X-rays too?
faq.a: Your dentist will recommend X-rays for children where clinically appropriate, such as monitoring developing teeth or assessing orthodontic needs.

faq.q: Will I need X-rays before other treatments, like implants or root canal?
faq.a: Yes, X-rays are typically part of the assessment and planning process for more involved treatments such as dental implants or root canal therapy.

check-ups-cleans.intro: Regular dental check-ups and professional cleans form the foundation of good oral health.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body:
While daily brushing and flossing go a long way, they can't reach every surface of your teeth or fully remove hardened plaque (tartar) that builds up over time. A routine visit to Footscray Dental Studio allows your dentist to assess the health of your teeth, gums and mouth, catch early signs of decay or gum disease before they become bigger problems, and keep your smile in the best possible condition.

At Footscray Dental Studio, we combine thorough clinical examination with modern diagnostic technology, including intraoral cameras and digital X-rays where needed, so you have a clear picture of your oral health at every visit.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
A typical check-up and clean at our practice generally includes:

  1. Examination — your dentist reviews your teeth, gums, tongue and soft tissue for signs of decay, gum disease, or other concerns.
  2. Diagnostic imaging (if needed) — digital X-rays or intraoral camera images may be taken to support a thorough assessment, particularly for areas not visible to the naked eye.
  3. Professional clean (scale and polish) — plaque and tartar build-up is carefully removed from your teeth, including areas that are difficult to reach with a toothbrush alone.
  4. Polishing — your teeth are polished to remove surface staining and leave a smooth, clean finish.
  5. Discussion and planning — your dentist talks you through any findings, answers your questions, and outlines next steps if further treatment is recommended.

sections.heading: Benefits of Regular Check-ups & Cleans
sections.body:
• Early identification of decay, gum disease and other oral health issues
  • Removal of plaque and tartar that home brushing can't fully address
  • An opportunity to ask questions and get professional guidance on your oral care routine
  • Reduced likelihood of needing more complex, costly treatment later
  • Peace of mind knowing your oral health is being actively monitored

sections.heading: Signs It May Be Time for a Visit
sections.body:
While we recommend regular check-ups regardless of symptoms, you should book a visit sooner if you notice:

  • Bleeding or swollen gums
  • Sensitivity to hot, cold or sweet foods
  • Visible discolouration, chips or cracks
  • Persistent bad breath
  • Discomfort when chewing

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Check-ups and cleans are recommended for patients of all ages as part of routine oral healthcare. Most patients are advised to visit every six months, though your dentist may suggest a different frequency depending on your individual oral health, risk factors, and dental history.

sections.heading: What to Expect During Your Visit
sections.body: Your appointment will be relaxed and unhurried — our team takes the time to explain what we're doing and why, so you always know what to expect. If any additional treatment is recommended, we'll walk you through your options clearly before proceeding, with no pressure to decide on the spot.

sections.heading: Caring for Your Teeth Between Visits
sections.body:
Maintaining good oral hygiene between appointments helps preserve the results of your professional clean and supports long-term oral health. This includes:

  • Brushing twice daily with fluoride toothpaste
  • Daily flossing or use of interdental brushes
  • Limiting sugary food and drinks
  • Attending your recommended check-up schedule
Book a Check-UpContact Us

faq.q: How long does a check-up and clean take?
faq.a: Appointment length can vary depending on individual needs, but a standard check-up and clean is typically a straightforward, single visit. Our team can give you a more specific estimate when you book.

faq.q: Is a professional clean painful?
faq.a: Most patients find a professional clean comfortable. If you experience sensitivity, let your dentist know so they can adjust their approach and make you more comfortable.

faq.q: Will I need X-rays at every check-up?
faq.a: Not necessarily — your dentist will recommend X-rays based on your dental history, risk factors and individual needs, rather than as a routine part of every single visit.

faq.q: How often should children have check-ups?
faq.a: Children are generally recommended to have check-ups every six months, similar to adults, allowing your dentist to monitor their developing teeth and provide early guidance on oral hygiene habits.

faq.q: What happens if a problem is found during my check-up?
faq.a: Your dentist will explain any findings clearly, discuss the available options, and help you decide on next steps — there's no obligation to proceed with treatment on the same day.

faq.q: Can I book a check-up and clean as a new patient?
faq.a: Yes — see our New Patient Exam & Clean offer, or contact us directly to book your first visit.

general-preventive.intro: Good oral health starts with prevention. Our general dentistry services are focused on maintaining healthy teeth and gums, identifying potential issues early, and helping you avoid more complex — and often more costly — treatment down the track.

sections.heading: What to Expect at Footscray Dental Studio
sections.body:
We recommend a check-up and clean every six months for most patients, though your dentist may suggest a different schedule based on your individual needs and risk factors.

At Footscray Dental Studio, our general and preventive services are supported by modern diagnostic technology, including digital X-rays, OPG imaging and intraoral cameras, giving your dentist a clear, detailed picture of your oral health at every visit.

Every general and preventive visit begins with a thorough assessment of your teeth, gums and overall oral health. Your dentist will explain any findings clearly, using diagnostic images where relevant, and talk you through recommended next steps without pressure. Whether you're due for a routine clean or need a specific concern investigated, our approach is the same: clear communication, thorough care, and a comfortable experience.

sections.heading: Why Preventive Care Matters
sections.body:
Preventive dentistry isn't just about avoiding pain — it's about protecting your long-term oral health and reducing the likelihood of needing more extensive, invasive treatment later. Small issues caught early, such as the beginnings of decay or early gum inflammation, are often far simpler and more comfortable to address than problems that have been left untreated.

Book an AppointmentContact Us

faq.q: How often should I have a check-up and clean?
faq.a: Most patients are recommended a check-up every six months, though your dentist may suggest a different interval based on your oral health and individual risk factors.

faq.q: Are X-rays needed at every visit?
faq.a: Not necessarily — your dentist will recommend X-rays based on your individual needs, dental history and any specific concerns, rather than as a routine part of every visit.

faq.q: Is preventive dentistry suitable for children?
faq.a: Yes, preventive care including fluoride treatments and fissure sealants is commonly recommended for children as their adult teeth come through, alongside regular check-ups.

faq.q: What happens if gum disease is found during a check-up?
faq.a: Your dentist will discuss appropriate treatment options with you, ranging from improved home care and professional cleaning to periodontal treatment, depending on severity.

faq.q: Can I combine a check-up with other treatments in one visit?
faq.a: This depends on your individual treatment plan and the complexity of any additional treatment — your dentist will let you know what can be scheduled together.

faq.q: Do you offer mouthguards for both sport and grinding?
faq.a: Yes, we offer custom-fitted mouthguards for sport as well as night guards for teeth grinding, tailored to your specific needs.

emergency-dentistry.intro: Dental emergencies can happen without warning — a sudden toothache, a knocked-out tooth from a fall, or a broken filling that leaves a tooth exposed and sensitive.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: When this happens, prompt attention can make a real difference to both your comfort and the outcome for your tooth. At Footscray Dental Studio, we aim to see emergency patients as quickly as possible during our opening hours.

sections.heading: What Counts as a Dental Emergency
sections.body:
Common dental emergencies include:

  • Severe or persistent tooth pain
  • A knocked-out (avulsed) tooth
  • A broken, cracked or chipped tooth
  • A lost filling or crown
  • Swelling in the face, gums or mouth
  • Bleeding that doesn't stop after an injury
  • A broken denture or orthodontic appliance causing discomfort

If you're unsure whether your situation counts as an emergency, please call us — our team can help assess the urgency and advise on next steps over the phone.

faq.q: What should I do if my tooth gets knocked out?
faq.a: Handle it by the crown, avoid touching the root, and try to reinsert it into the socket if possible. If not, keep it moist in milk or saliva and come in as soon as possible — timing matters for the best chance of saving the tooth.

faq.q: Do you offer same-day emergency appointments?
faq.a: We aim to see emergency patients as promptly as possible within our opening hours — please call ahead so our team can prepare for your visit.

faq.q: What if I have a dental emergency outside your opening hours?
faq.a: Please contact your nearest hospital emergency department or after-hours medical service for urgent care outside our opening hours.

faq.q: Is a toothache always an emergency?
faq.a: Severe or persistent pain should be assessed promptly, as it can indicate infection or other issues needing timely treatment — call us and our team can help assess urgency.

faq.q: Can a knocked-out tooth always be saved?
faq.a: This depends on factors including how quickly it's treated and how the tooth was cared for in the meantime — prompt attention gives the best chance of a positive outcome.

faq.q: Should I go to a hospital or a dentist for a dental emergency?
faq.a: For most dental emergencies, contacting our practice directly is the right first step. For severe trauma, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or significant blood loss, please seek emergency medical care immediately.

emergency-dentistry.banner: If you're experiencing a dental emergency, please call us directly on (03) 9000 0792.
emergency-dentistry.wait_heading: What to Do While You Wait to Be Seen

wait_cards.title: Knocked-out tooth
wait_cards.text: Handle the tooth by the crown (the white part), not the root. If possible, gently rinse it without scrubbing and try to reinsert it into the socket. If that isn't possible, keep it moist — in milk or your saliva — and get to us as soon as possible, as timing can affect the chance of saving the tooth.

wait_cards.title: Severe toothache
wait_cards.text: Rinse your mouth with warm water. A cold compress against the outside of your cheek may help with discomfort. Avoid placing aspirin directly against the gum or tooth.

wait_cards.title: Broken or chipped tooth
wait_cards.text: Rinse your mouth with warm water and, if possible, save any broken tooth fragments. A cold compress can help reduce swelling.

wait_cards.title: Lost filling or crown
wait_cards.text: If you still have the crown, keep it safe and bring it with you. Avoid chewing on the affected side until you're seen.

wait_cards.title: Swelling or facial trauma
wait_cards.text: Apply a cold compress to the outside of the affected area and contact us promptly, as swelling can sometimes indicate infection requiring urgent attention.

emergency-dentistry.wait_note: This guidance is general in nature and doesn't replace professional dental or medical advice. If you're experiencing severe symptoms, difficulty breathing or swallowing, or significant facial trauma, please seek emergency medical care immediately.

For dental emergencies outside these hours, please contact your nearest hospital emergency department or after-hours medical service.

veneers.intro: Porcelain veneers are thin, custom-made shells designed to be bonded to the front surface of your teeth.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: They're commonly used to address a range of cosmetic concerns, including chips, gaps, discolouration that doesn't respond well to whitening, or irregularly shaped teeth. At Footscray Dental Studio, veneers are planned individually for each patient, following a consultation to assess your teeth and discuss your goals.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
The process for porcelain veneers generally includes:

  1. Consultation — your dentist examines your teeth and discusses your goals, explaining whether veneers are a suitable option for you.
  2. Planning — your treatment is planned, including the number of veneers, shape and shade, often supported by digital smile photography.
  3. Tooth preparation — a small amount of enamel is typically prepared to accommodate the veneer, ensuring a natural fit.
  4. Digital impressions — a digital scan captures the precise shape needed for your custom veneers.
  5. Fabrication — your veneers are custom-made, often by a dental laboratory, to match your specifications.
  6. Fitting — once ready, your veneers are carefully bonded into place and checked for fit and comfort.

sections.heading: Benefits of Porcelain Veneers
sections.body:
• Can address multiple cosmetic concerns (shape, colour, minor gaps) in one coordinated treatment
  • Porcelain is stain-resistant compared with natural enamel
  • Custom-made to fit your individual teeth and desired outcome
  • Can be planned as part of a broader smile makeover if multiple teeth are involved

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Veneers may be suitable for patients with cosmetic concerns such as chips, gaps, wear, or discolouration who have generally healthy teeth and gums. As veneers involve some preparation of the natural tooth, your dentist will assess whether this is an appropriate and suitable option for your particular situation, or whether an alternative such as composite bonding may be more appropriate.

sections.heading: Caring for Your Veneers
sections.body:
Veneers are generally cared for in the same way as natural teeth — regular brushing, flossing and check-ups. Your dentist may also recommend a night guard if you grind your teeth, to help protect your veneers over time.

Book a Veneers ConsultationContact Us

faq.q: How many veneers will I need?
faq.a: This depends on your individual goals and the teeth involved — your dentist will discuss this with you during your consultation.

faq.q: Is getting veneers painful?
faq.a: The process typically involves local anaesthetic for tooth preparation, and most patients report discomfort is well managed — your dentist will discuss what to expect for your specific treatment.

faq.q: How long do porcelain veneers last?
faq.a: Longevity varies by individual, depending on factors such as oral hygiene, diet, and habits like teeth grinding — your dentist can discuss what to expect based on your circumstances.

faq.q: Can veneers be whitened later?
faq.a: No, porcelain veneers don't respond to whitening treatments in the way natural teeth do — your dentist will discuss shade planning carefully before your veneers are made.

faq.q: What's the difference between veneers and composite bonding?
faq.a: Veneers are custom-fabricated porcelain shells requiring some tooth preparation, while composite bonding uses a resin material applied directly to the tooth — your dentist can advise which suits your situation.

faq.q: Can veneers be part of a smile makeover?
faq.a: Yes, veneers are commonly included as part of a broader smile makeover plan alongside other treatments where appropriate.

teeth-whitening.intro: Over time, teeth can become discoloured due to factors such as food and drink, smoking, ageing, or certain medications.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: Professional teeth whitening is one of the most straightforward ways to address surface and deeper staining, using controlled, dentist-supervised methods rather than generic over-the-counter products. At Footscray Dental Studio, we offer whitening options tailored to your individual needs following a thorough consultation.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
Professional whitening at our practice generally involves:

  1. Consultation and assessment — your dentist examines your teeth and gums to confirm you're a suitable candidate and discusses your goals.
  2. Shade assessment — your current tooth shade is recorded so progress can be tracked.
  3. Treatment — depending on the option recommended, whitening may be carried out in-chair, via a take-home kit, or a combination of both.
  4. Review — your dentist checks the outcome and discusses any touch-up or maintenance options.

sections.heading: Whitening Options
sections.body:
• In-chair whitening — a professionally applied treatment carried out at the practice under dentist supervision.
  • Take-home whitening — custom-fitted trays and professional-strength whitening gel for use at home, following your dentist's instructions.

Your dentist will recommend the option best suited to your teeth, goals, and lifestyle.

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Teeth whitening is generally suitable for patients with staining or discolouration who are in good general oral health. It isn't suitable for everyone — for example, patients with certain existing dental work, untreated decay, or gum disease may need other issues addressed first. Whitening results can also vary between individuals depending on the type and cause of staining. Your dentist will confirm your suitability at consultation.

sections.heading: What to Expect Afterwards
sections.body:
Some temporary sensitivity is common after whitening treatment. Your dentist will provide guidance on caring for your teeth afterwards, including any dietary recommendations to help maintain your results.

Book a Whitening ConsultationContact Us

faq.q: How long does teeth whitening take?
faq.a: This depends on the method used — in-chair whitening is typically completed in a single visit, while take-home whitening is used over a period at home as directed by your dentist.

faq.q: Is teeth whitening painful?
faq.a: Some patients experience temporary tooth sensitivity during or after treatment, which your dentist can help manage.

faq.q: How long do results last?
faq.a: This varies between individuals depending on diet, habits such as smoking, and oral hygiene — your dentist can discuss what to expect and how to help maintain your results.

faq.q: Is teeth whitening safe?
faq.a: Professional whitening carried out under dentist supervision is a widely used cosmetic treatment; your dentist will confirm suitability for your specific teeth and oral health.

faq.q: Will whitening work on crowns or veneers?
faq.a: No, whitening only affects natural tooth enamel — existing crowns, veneers or fillings won't change colour, which your dentist will discuss if relevant to your treatment plan.

faq.q: Can I choose how white my teeth become?
faq.a: Your dentist will discuss achievable and appropriate shade options with you as part of your consultation, based on your natural teeth and treatment type.

smile-makeovers.intro: For patients considering more than one cosmetic or restorative treatment, a smile makeover approach allows everything to be planned together, rather than addressed one treatment at a time.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: This coordinated planning process helps ensure the various elements of your treatment work well together, both functionally and aesthetically.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
A smile makeover consultation at our practice generally includes:

  1. In-depth consultation — your dentist discusses your goals, concerns, and any previous dental history in detail.
  2. Comprehensive assessment — including digital photography, X-rays, and a digital scan where appropriate, to build a complete picture of your teeth and bite.
  3. Treatment planning — your dentist develops a coordinated plan, which may combine treatments such as whitening, veneers, bonding, crowns, or implants, depending on your individual needs.
  4. Staged treatment — treatment is carried out in a logical sequence, which your dentist will explain clearly from the outset, including expected timeframes.
  5. Review — your progress is reviewed throughout treatment, with adjustments made as needed.

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: A smile makeover approach may suit patients considering multiple treatments, those with more complex cosmetic or functional concerns, or anyone who would prefer a single, coordinated plan rather than making decisions treatment-by-treatment. Your dentist will discuss whether this approach is appropriate for your situation, or whether a single, standalone treatment may better suit your needs and goals.

sections.heading: What to Expect During the Process
sections.body:
Because a smile makeover can involve multiple treatments and visits, your dentist will provide a clear overview of the proposed plan, expected timeframe, and what each stage involves before you commit to proceeding. You'll have the opportunity to ask questions and adjust the plan as needed at each stage.

composite-bonding.intro: Composite bonding uses a tooth-coloured resin material, carefully applied and shaped to address minor cosmetic concerns such as small chips, gaps, or irregularly shaped teeth.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: It's a more conservative option than veneers, as it typically requires little to no removal of natural tooth structure, and can often be completed in a single visit.

sections.heading: What's Involved
sections.body:
Composite bonding at our practice generally includes:

  1. Consultation — your dentist assesses your teeth and discusses whether bonding is a suitable option for your concerns.
  2. Shade matching — the composite resin is matched to the natural shade of your surrounding teeth.
  3. Application — the resin material is applied in layers and shaped to achieve the desired result.
  4. Curing — each layer is hardened using a curing light.
  5. Shaping and polishing — the bonded material is shaped and polished to blend naturally with your existing teeth.

sections.heading: Benefits of Composite Bonding
sections.body:
• Often completed in a single visit
  • Minimal to no removal of natural tooth structure required
  • A more conservative and reversible option compared with veneers
  • Can be used to address small chips, gaps, or shape irregularities

sections.heading: Who It's Suitable For
sections.body: Composite bonding may be suitable for patients with minor cosmetic concerns who are looking for a more conservative treatment option. It may not be suitable for larger corrections or more significant concerns, where veneers or other treatments might be more appropriate. Your dentist will assess your teeth and discuss the most suitable option for your goals.

sections.heading: Caring for Bonded Teeth
sections.body:
Composite material can be more prone to staining and chipping than porcelain over time, so your dentist may provide specific guidance on diet and care to help maintain your bonding. Regular check-ups allow your dentist to monitor the condition of the bonded areas.

Book a Bonding ConsultationContact Us

faq.q: How long does composite bonding take?
faq.a: Many bonding treatments can be completed in a single visit, though this depends on the number of teeth involved and the extent of the work.

faq.q: Is composite bonding painful?
faq.a: Bonding is generally a comfortable procedure, often requiring little to no anaesthetic — your dentist will explain what to expect for your specific treatment.

faq.q: How long does composite bonding last?
faq.a: Longevity varies between patients depending on habits such as diet and teeth grinding — your dentist can discuss what to expect and how to help it last.

faq.q: Can composite bonding be repaired if it chips?
faq.a: In many cases, minor chips to bonded areas can be repaired — your dentist will assess this on a case-by-case basis.

faq.q: Is bonding a permanent treatment?
faq.a: Bonding is generally considered a more conservative and reversible option compared with veneers, though it will need monitoring and maintenance over time.

faq.q: What's the difference between bonding and veneers?
faq.a: Bonding uses a resin material applied directly to the tooth with minimal preparation, while veneers are custom-fabricated porcelain shells requiring some tooth preparation — your dentist can advise which is more suitable for you.

childrens-dentistry.intro: Establishing good dental habits early helps set children up for a lifetime of healthy teeth and gums.

sections.heading: What you should know
sections.body: At Footscray Dental Studio, we provide a calm, welcoming environment for young patients, with a focus on making visits comfortable and positive from their very first appointment. Our team takes the time to explain things in a way children can understand, helping to build confidence around dental visits rather than apprehension.

sections.heading: Our Approach to Treating Children
sections.body: We understand that a child's early experiences at the dentist can shape how they feel about oral care for years to come. Our team takes a gentle, patient approach, explaining each step in simple terms and adjusting our pace to suit each child's comfort level. Parents and carers are welcome to stay with their child throughout the appointment.

sections.heading: Services for Children
sections.body:
• Check-ups & Cleans — regular examinations to monitor developing teeth and catch any concerns early
  • Fluoride Treatments — helping strengthen developing enamel and reduce decay risk
  • Fissure Sealants — a protective coating for the chewing surfaces of new adult molars
  • Digital X-Rays — low-radiation imaging where needed to monitor tooth development
  • Mouthguards — custom-fitted sport mouthguards for children playing contact sports

sections.heading: When to Bring Your Child for Their First Visit
sections.body: It's generally recommended that children have their first dental visit around the time their first teeth appear, or by their first birthday, allowing your dentist to monitor early development and offer guidance to parents on caring for young teeth. Regular six-monthly check-ups are then generally recommended as your child grows, though your dentist may suggest a different schedule based on individual needs.

sections.heading: Common Concerns We Help With
sections.body:
• Monitoring the eruption of baby teeth and later adult teeth
  • Early signs of decay, particularly in young children who may still be developing brushing habits
  • Guidance on thumb-sucking, dummy use, and their effects on developing teeth
  • Preparing anxious children for a comfortable dental experience
  • Sports-related mouthguards for active children and teenagers

sections.heading: Child Dental Benefits Schedule (CDBS)
sections.body:
Eligible children may be entitled to bulk-billed dental services under the Child Dental Benefits Schedule, a government program supporting access to essential dental care for children. Contact us to check your child's eligibility.

sections.heading: Tips for Parents Between Visits
sections.body:
• Encourage brushing twice daily with an age-appropriate fluoride toothpaste
  • Supervise brushing until children can reliably do it well on their own, generally around age 7–8
  • Limit sugary food and drinks, particularly between meals
  • Lead by example — children often mirror parents' own oral hygiene habits

faq.q: When should my child have their first dental visit?

about.story:
Welcome to Footscray Dental Studio — a fresh, modern chapter for a practice with a strong foundation in the local community. The practice is now under new management, building on the foundations of EZY Dental Group while bringing fresh leadership, experience and a genuine commitment to making every patient's dental experience comfortable, personalised and positive.

Our team has been providing dental services to the local community for many years, with a strong focus on quality care, patient relationships and positive dental experiences. Together, our practitioners bring more than 20 years of combined experience across general and comprehensive dental services.

We believe great dentistry is about more than treating teeth — it's about getting to know our patients, understanding their individual needs, and helping them feel comfortable and confident in their care. As your local dental studio, we're proud to be part of the Footscray community and look forward to caring for generations of patients and families.

Whether you're visiting for a routine check-up, preventive care, or more comprehensive treatment, our team is here to provide professional care with a warm, personalised approach.

Formerly Ezy Dental Group. Footscray Dental Studio is the same practice, at the same address on Barkly St, with many of the same familiar faces. The name and leadership have changed; our commitment to the Footscray community has not.
about.philosophy_text:
Our philosophy is simple — we want every patient to feel comfortable, respected and genuinely cared for. We take the time to listen, understand each patient's needs, and provide clear, honest advice so they can make informed decisions about their dental health.

We believe dentistry should be personal, preventive and focused on long-term wellbeing. Our approach combines clinical experience and modern dentistry with a warm, approachable environment where patients feel at ease.

We're committed to building lasting relationships with our patients and families, rather than simply providing treatment. For us, success is seeing our patients leave feeling confident about their oral health, knowing they have a dental team they can trust. As a local practice, we're proud to be part of the Footscray community and look forward to caring for our patients for many years to come.

about.continuity_text:
We highly value the contribution and experience of every member of our existing team. As part of the transition to new leadership, several of our existing practitioners and support staff continue with the practice, providing continuity and familiarity for our patients.

At the same time, we've welcomed additional experienced practitioners to the team, strengthening our clinical capabilities and broadening the range of services available — so we can better support the diverse dental needs of the local community. Our focus is on retaining the strengths and relationships that already exist within the practice, while introducing new expertise, ideas and capabilities under new leadership.
